topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer etiology and the interplay of genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer arises through somatic mutations and microenvironmental support, assessing the relative contributions of intrinsic biological chance, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures across populations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of initiation, metabolic activation, and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical and cellular mechanisms through which environmental agents damage DNA, undergo host metabolic activation, and act as tumor promoters or initiators across susceptible tissues.

topics.label: Methods for determining carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the experimental, sequencing, and epidemiological approaches used to identify carcinogens and their mutagenic signatures, concluding with practical risk-benefit considerations.
